author: EmuCore - Hub
title: DuckStation adds a 4x2 scanline grid built for non-integer scaling
summary: Scanline Modern 4x2 aligns its pattern to physical display pixels, adapts around source-pixel edges, and varies strength with perceived brightness instead of drawing the same stripes everywhere.
heroAlt: Visual evidence from DuckStation pull request #3755: feat(shader): add Scanline Modern 4x2 adaptive retro filter

sourceLabels.duckstation-pr-3755: feat(shader): add Scanline Modern 4x2 adaptive retro filter

blocks.text: Rigid scanlines expose the uneven cadence of non-integer scaling

A PlayStation image rarely maps to a modern 1440p or 4K panel with an exact integer ratio in both directions. Repeating a simple dark stripe over that result can emphasize unequal source-pixel widths rather than disguise them. Scanline Modern 4x2 approaches the problem in physical output pixels, establishing a repeating four-by-two grid that stays stable even when the virtual pixel grid lands between panel pixels.
Edge detection protects text from the fixed physical pattern

The shader detects sub-pixel alignment near sharp source edges and adjusts the mask where virtual pixels do not map one-to-one. That step matters for menus and pixel fonts, where a fixed overlay can make one stroke darker than its neighbor. The filter is therefore not only a cosmetic crosshatch: the output grid remains fixed, while local edge information controls how strongly it is allowed to interfere with high-contrast detail.
Perceptual luma moves scanlines away from highlights and deep shadows

Scanline amplitude peaks in mid-tones and rolls off toward extreme brightness and darkness. This follows the stated perceptual goal of showing structure where the eye can read it without crushing shadow detail or visibly striping highlights. The 4x2 edition also hardcodes its parameter matrix rather than evaluating periodic sin() functions, trading broad configurability for a specialized, cheaper preset.
Display-resolution testing must include motion and fine UI

The source reports tests on 1080p, 1440p, and 2160p LCDs with high-resolution internal rendering and both low-poly and sprite-based titles. Review should add scrolling text, slow camera pans, checkerboards, and one-pixel UI lines at several non-integer window sizes. Capture the unfiltered image too, and verify brightness, color, shimmer, and frame time; a pleasing static screenshot can still conceal unstable motion or excessive GPU cost.
The filter's identity is the fixed physical 4x2 grid; edge and luma adaptation keep that grid from becoming more visible than the game.
